role_in_parent: Converts pointwise nonpositivity of the derivative into a nonpositive integral.
statement_nl: Let f : ℝ → ℝ and let d be a nonnegative real number. If f is differentiable on [0,d] and its derivative is ≤ 0 at every point of [0,d], then the interval integral of its derivative from 0 to d is ≤ 0.

domain_restrictions: d is a nonnegative real number
f is differentiable at every point of the closed interval [0,d]
the derivative value f prime of x is defined and is a real number for every x in [0,d]
the integral from 0 to d of f prime of x is well-defined in the intended integration sense
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every function f from real numbers to real numbers and every real number d with d >= 0, if f is differentiable on the closed interval from 0 to d and for every real number x in [0,d] the derivative of f at x is at most 0, then the integral from 0 to d of the derivative of f is at most 0.
quantifier_order: For all functions f from real numbers to real numbers
For all real numbers d with d >= 0
Assume for all real numbers x with x in the closed interval [0,d], the derivative of f at x is at most 0
Then the integral from 0 to d of the derivative of f is at most 0

variables.name: f
variables.role: input-output map; differentiable on the interval [0,d]

variables.name: d
variables.role: right endpoint of the integration/differentiability interval

variables.name: x
variables.role: generic point where the derivative condition is assumed
